items.stem: A screen mixes UI rendering, business rules and direct network calls in one class, making it hard to test. Which principle most directly addresses this?

options.rationale: Correct: separating UI, logic and data into layers makes each independently testable and maintainable.
More globals increase coupling and worsen testability.
Removing structure makes the tangle worse, not better.

options.text: Rendering the screen on a background thread
options.rationale: Threading does not address the mixing of responsibilities.

items.explanation: Correct: separating UI, logic and data into layers makes each independently testable and maintainable.

items.stem: Which TWO are benefits of unidirectional data flow with a single source of truth? (Select TWO.)

options.text: State changes are predictable and easier to trace
options.rationale: Correct: one-way flow makes it clear how and where state changes.

options.text: There is one authoritative copy of state to reason about
options.rationale: Correct: a single source of truth avoids divergent copies.

options.text: It guarantees the app needs no network code
options.rationale: Data flow design is unrelated to whether networking exists.

options.text: It removes the need for any state at all
options.rationale: State still exists; it is organised, not eliminated.

items.explanation: Correct: one-way flow makes it clear how and where state changes.

items.stem: Why introduce a repository between the UI and the data sources?

options.text: It gives the UI one interface and hides whether data comes from cache or network
options.rationale: Correct: the repository abstracts data sources so the UI depends on an interface, aiding testing and caching.

options.text: It makes the UI call the database directly
options.rationale: A repository exists precisely to stop the UI calling data sources directly.

options.text: It removes the need for any remote data
options.rationale: Repositories coordinate remote and local data; they do not remove remote data.

options.text: It is only a naming convention with no effect
options.rationale: It changes dependencies and testability, not just naming.

items.explanation: Correct: the repository abstracts data sources so the UI depends on an interface, aiding testing and caching.
